lettering: The earlier grid uses nine contrasting task views to explain plurality. Those exact views were not preserved together. lettering: Communication can let one run use another’s findings; storage can preserve work; access can widen the actions available. Each benefit depends on a working mechanism and usable evidence. A copied answer can also spread a mistake. The diagram supplies no guarantee of correct information, successful access or saved effort.

lettering: Different assigned goals can create overlapping demands. Shared resources do not establish identical goals, agreement, a collective mind or universal need. Nor does the fact that some agents have duplicate tasks justify claiming that every participant began with the same objective.
